meta.title: Mentari: solar certificates on two ledgers
meta.description: Solar watt-hour certificates on QoreChain testnet. Each retirement burns on the EVM and writes a Native receipt in the same transaction.
meta.imageAlt: Mentari: a yellow sun rising over the horizon, with the site title and summary.

data.sample: Local fixture for development. These numbers are examples, not measurements from the testnet.

registry.title: Solar watt-hours, recorded on two ledgers at once
registry.lede: Each Mentari certificate is one watt-hour from a solar meter. Retiring one burns it on the EVM and writes a receipt on the Native ledger in the same transaction. If either side fails, neither changes.
registry.agreeDetail: The latest {checked} of {total} retirements each have a matching receipt.
registry.disagreeDetail: {failed} of the latest {checked} retirements have no matching receipt.
registry.emptyDetail: The first retirement will show here with its receipt.
registry.errorDetail: The testnet did not answer. The page tries again in {seconds} seconds.

systems.title: Solar systems
systems.note: These meters are simulated. Readings come from a seeded model, are signed with ML-DSA-87 keys and are checked by the contract like real readings.
systems.name: Meter {label}

how.title: One transaction, two virtual machines
how.lede: Mentari keeps its certificates on the EVM and its receipts on the Native ledger. Retiring a certificate touches both, and the chain treats it as one transaction.
how.step1: You call retire on the Mentari contract with an amount and a short memo.
how.step2: The contract burns your certificates first.
how.step3: It calls the Cross-VM bridge at {bridge} with a record message.
how.step4: The Native receipts book stores the note and returns a receipt id.
how.step5: The contract checks that the id is newer than the last one, then stores the retirement.
how.fail: If any step fails, the whole transaction reverts. No burn, no receipt.
how.diagramLabel: Diagram of one retirement crossing from the EVM to the Native ledger and back.
how.noteBody: The contract builds the note itself from typed fields. The memo is limited to letters, digits, spaces and . : / # -, so a memo cannot change the message.
how.keysBody: Meter readings are signed with ML-DSA-87 and checked on chain by the pqcVerify precompile. Certificates can only move to accounts that have a registered ML-DSA-87 key.
how.limit1: The meters are simulated. Nothing here comes from a real solar panel.
how.limit2: This runs on QoreChain testnet. Certificates have no value.
how.limit3: Other projects use the same receipts book, so its total count includes their receipts. Each Mentari retirement is checked by its own receipt id.
how.limit4: The page checks the latest {n} retirements on each visit, not the whole history.
how.limit5: The contracts cannot be upgraded. A fix means a new deployment at a new address.

records.txUnknown: No EVM transaction found: it was sent from the Native ledger, or the node limits log searches
records.noReceipt: The Native ledger has no receipt with this id.

retirements.title: Every retirement, on both ledgers
retirements.lede: Each row is one transaction. The left side is what the Mentari contract stored on the EVM. The right side is the receipt the same transaction wrote on the Native ledger. The page reads both and compares them.
retirements.empty: No retirement to list here. Each new one shows with its receipt.

verify.title: Check one retirement
verify.lede: Enter a retirement number or a receipt id. The page reads the EVM record and the Native receipt from testnet and checks that they point to each other. The address of this page is the result, so you can share it.
verify.invalid: Enter a whole number from 1 up.
verify.noRetirement: The contract has no retirement with this number yet.
verify.noReceipt: The Native ledger has no receipt with this id.
verify.orphan: This receipt names retirement #{n}, but the contract has no such retirement.
verify.notMentari: This receipt exists, but the Mentari contract did not write it. It was sent by {sender}.

check.receiptExists: The Native ledger has the receipt
check.sameId: The EVM record and the receipt point to each other
check.sender: The receipt was written by the Mentari contract
check.note: The receipt note names this retirement, amount and holder

tryit.title: Try it on testnet
tryit.lede: These buttons send real testnet transactions from a demo account. One succeeds and changes both ledgers. Three are built to fail and change neither.
tryit.guideTitle: Check the claim in three steps
tryit.step1: Press Retire now. One transaction burns {wh} Wh on the EVM and writes a receipt on the Native ledger. Both counts go up by one.
tryit.step2: Press any of the three failure buttons. Each transaction reaches the Native side and then fails. Both counts stay the same.
tryit.step3: Open the transaction in the explorer, or check the new retirement on the Verify page.
tryit.statusLoading: Checking whether live sends are open.
tryit.statusOffline: Live sends are not available right now. Each button shows the recorded testnet case instead.
tryit.statusDisabled: Live sends are switched off. Each button shows the recorded testnet case instead.
tryit.statusLive: Live sends are open. {today} left today, {you} left for you this hour.
tryit.retireNowSub: Burn {wh} Wh and write one receipt
tryit.failLede: Each of these touches the Native ledger inside the transaction and then fails. If the chain is atomic, nothing is kept.

case-b.label: Write, then revert
case-b.what: A receipt is written, then the EVM side reverts

case-c.label: Native side refuses
case-c.what: The receipts book rejects the message

case-d.label: Call a blocked contract
case-d.what: The target is not on the bridge allowlist

tryit.expectSuccess: Both ledgers should go up by one.
tryit.nativeRoute: Sent from the Native ledger as one transaction, signed with both secp256k1 and ML-DSA-87. It ran Mentari.retire on the EVM, which wrote the receipt back on the Native ledger. No EVM access window was needed.

wallet.title: Retire from your own wallet
wallet.lede: Connect QoreX, ask the demo account for {wh} Wh of certificates, then retire them yourself. Your transaction writes the receipt to the Native ledger, the same way Retire now does.
wallet.honest: QoreX signs Native transactions today. It does not sign EVM transactions yet, so it may refuse the last step. Retire now above needs no wallet.
wallet.wrongNetwork: Your wallet is on another network. Switch QoreX to the QoreChain testnet.
wallet.readyYes: Yes. An ML-DSA-87 key is registered.
wallet.readyNo: No ML-DSA-87 key yet. Register one in QoreX first.
wallet.notDeployed: This build has no contract address, so these steps are closed. Connecting works.
wallet.grantSent: The demo account sent you {wh} Wh:

problem.declined: You declined the request in your wallet. Nothing was sent.
problem.unsupported: QoreX refused to sign this EVM transaction. It does not sign EVM transactions yet. Nothing was sent.
problem.not-quantum-ready: The contract only pays accounts with a registered ML-DSA-87 key. Register one in QoreX, then try again.
problem.insufficient: Your wallet holds fewer certificates than this retires. Get {wh} Wh first.
problem.failed: The transaction did not go through. Nothing was kept.
